minutes.headline: Board favors ARPA funds for ambulance and two plow trucks; vote deferred to Feb 21 for finance committee input.
minutes.summary: The meeting covered public concern over the 2023 property assessments and the board's investigation, a town manager report, and a preliminary FY24 capital plan. The board discussed ARPA spending categories and leaned toward using ARPA for the ambulance and two plow trucks, deferring a vote to February 21. Two civilian traffic members were ratified unanimously, and a short-term rental ban got little support.

what_happened.line: The Select Board leaned toward paying for the ambulance and two plow trucks with ARPA money but deferred the vote to February 21 for finance committee input.
A majority declined to use ARPA for burial and cremation costs, and the chair declined to support ARPA staff bonuses.
The town manager presented a preliminary FY24 capital plan of prioritized projects, with the replacement ambulance as top priority.
Residents pressed the board on the 2023 property assessments and the investigation into them, and one group said it will retain an attorney.
The board ratified two civilian traffic members unanimously by roll call; a majority did not support asking the planning board to draft a short-term rental ban.

why_it_matters: Using ARPA, which is one-time federal money, for the ambulance and trucks would keep those purchases off the tax levy, and the February vote will set how much of the remaining ARPA balance is spent on them.
Residents with questions about their 2023 assessments will see the investigation and any abatement requests continue to be raised at board meetings.
watch_next: February 21: Select Board vote on using ARPA for the ambulance and two plow trucks, with the Parks Commissioners asked to return revised numbers and a funding plan.
The February 14 meeting is skipped; the board next meets February 28.
